q: How do I calculate water withdrawal, consumption and water intensity for BRSR?
title: Water withdrawal and intensity for BRSR
short: Add up all water drawn in the year by source, in kilolitres: that is withdrawal. Subtract water discharged to get consumption. Divide consumption by revenue from operations for intensity per rupee, and by revenue converted at the PPP rate for the BRSR Core figure. Report a physical output intensity too if it suits your sector.
audience: Listed companies and their value-chain suppliers in India

sections.h: Withdrawal: what goes in each source line
ul: Surface water: drawn from a river, lake or canal under your own permission.
Groundwater: borewells and open wells on your premises, from flow meter readings.
Third party water: municipal supply, industrial estate supply and tanker water.
Others: any source that fits none of the above; say what it is.
p: Report every figure in kilolitres for the financial year. Water recycled inside the plant through your ETP or RO is not new withdrawal; count it once, when it first comes in.

Work out consumption as withdrawal minus discharge, the same definition GRI 303 uses. Discharge is reported by destination (surface water, groundwater, seawater, third parties such as a CETP or sewer) and by level of treatment. A unit with zero liquid discharge reports little or no discharge, so its consumption is close to its withdrawal.
Water that leaves in product or evaporates in cooling towers and evaporators is consumed.

ol: Per rupee of turnover: total consumption in kL / revenue from operations in rupees. Many companies also show it per crore for readability.

BRSR Core: consumption / revenue from operations adjusted for purchasing power parity, using the latest PPP rate for India published by the IMF and disclosing the rate used, as the industry standards note for BRSR Core asks, so it can be compared across countries.
Physical output: kL per tonne, per piece or per unit of product, where the company chooses a relevant metric and states it.

ul: Calibrated flow meters on each borewell and incoming line, with monthly logs.
Municipal and estate water bills, and tanker delivery slips with volumes.
Outlet meter readings and CETP or sewer charge invoices for discharge.
The revenue figure used, matched to the annual report, and the PPP rate with its source and year.

example.title: Worked example: a mid-size listed manufacturer
lines: Withdrawal: groundwater 80,000 kL + third party 40,000 kL = 1,20,000 kL
Discharge to CETP: 30,000 kL; consumption: 1,20,000 minus 30,000 = 90,000 kL
Revenue from operations: ₹300 crore; intensity: 90,000 / 300 = 300 kL per crore, or 0.00003 kL per rupee
PPP rate (illustrative): 20.5 rupees per international dollar; revenue = ₹3,00,00,00,000 / 20.5 = about 146.3 million PPP dollars
BRSR Core intensity: 90,000 / 146.3 = about 615 kL per million PPP dollars
example.note: The PPP rate is illustrative. Use the rate for the reporting year from the source your assurance provider accepts.
